executive_summary: Collection window February 8-14, 2028: New York Fashion Week Fall/Winter 2028 women's shows opened within this window, on the calendar confirmed in the 2028-02-07 report. Proenza Schouler's own site published the house's runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 show at New York Fashion Week, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a spiral-seam wrap coat -- a coat whose main seam spirals diagonally around the torso rather than running vertically down the front or side, producing an asymmetric closure line -- as a recurring construction across multiple looks. This is treated as genuine cross-sector corroboration: one designer_origin source (the house's own lookbook, describing its own runway as designer intent) and one editorial source doing independent runway-review reporting, not a restatement of the house's own materials. Per derive_confidence(), corroboration_count=2 spanning two distinct sectors yields 'high'; this is adopted as computed, applying the same reasoning already used for the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton and 2028-01-31 Dior signals. This remains designer intent (a specific construction shown on one house's runway) reported through one designer-origin channel and one independent editorial review; it is not yet a claim of editorial-consensus interpretation across other houses, retail adoption, or social amplification, none of which have occurred yet within this window. No retail, social, resale, independent-criticism, or institutional source introduced a development distinct from this runway coverage this week. The resort 2028 puffer-shell skirt thread, the resale-demand signal on structured waist-tailoring, the obi-sash cocoon coat thread, and the opera-glove/'restraint dressing' thread all produced no new development this window and are not carried forward again absent fresh movement. The Margiela raw-edge thread remains closed out as of 2027-10-18. Met Gala 2027, Wales Bonner, and CFDA's Fashion Fund/Awards remain untracked going forward per standing convention.
